1.mascotDialogue: extract-max is really two moves: swap the root with the last leaf, shrink the heap by one, then let that displaced value sink to wherever it actually belongs.

2.mascotDialogue: Lines 4 and 5 find the biggest of the node and its two children. Line 8's recursive call lets the displaced value keep sinking past more than one level if it needs to.

3.mascotDialogue: 9 sits up top, and every parent down this tree beats both its children — same array-index arithmetic as min heap, just the comparison flipped.

4.mascotDialogue: The swap alone doesn't finish the job. Without siftDown you've merely relocated the problem to the top of the tree rather than solved it.
